title: Guest browsing Find Mentors triggers an infinite reload loop
description: GET /reviews and GET /availability were fully auth-gated, and the frontend axios interceptor reloaded the page on ANY 401 response, including a guest's who never had a token to refresh in the first place.
steps_to_reproduce: As a guest (no login), go to Find Mentors, click View or Book on any mentor card.
expected: Mentor profile / booking page loads normally.
actual: Page loads, 401s, reloads, loops indefinitely.

title: Mentee interview completion links to a 404 dashboard route
description: The frontend called a removed/nonexistent endpoint to finalize the interview->dashboard hand-off after AI interview completion.
steps_to_reproduce: Complete the mentee AI interview end to end and follow the resulting link to the dashboard.
expected: Mentee lands on their dashboard with the interview-derived profile visible.
actual: 404 — the linking endpoint no longer existed.

title: CV parsing merges multi-line education/company text into garbage strings
description: The CV structured-data extractor's line-context window mis-handled degree/institution/company text spanning multiple lines, producing corrupted multi-line concatenations.
steps_to_reproduce: Upload a CV whose education or work-experience section has degree, institution, and dates on separate lines.
expected: Education/company fields extracted as clean, separate values.
actual: Fields corrupted by unrelated adjacent lines being concatenated in.

title: CV parsing never populated title/industry fields
description: MentorProfile.title and MentorProfile.industry were never actually mapped from the CV headline extraction, despite the schema and UI expecting them.
steps_to_reproduce: Upload a CV with a clear professional-title headline (e.g. 'Senior Software Engineer') and build the mentor profile.
expected: title and industry populate on the mentor profile.
actual: Both fields stayed null regardless of CV content.

title: AI_interviewer and Rag_Chatbot both default to port 8000
description: Both Python services hardcode port 8000 as their default uvicorn port, colliding when both must run simultaneously for full app coverage (mentee interview + chatbot widget).
steps_to_reproduce: Start AI_interviewer and Rag_Chatbot both with default settings.
expected: Both services start and bind their own port.
actual: The second service fails to bind (port already in use).

title: Rag_Chatbot fails to start — unresolved git merge conflict committed as source
description: backend/Rag_Chatbot/app/core/config.py had literal <<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>> conflict markers committed directly, causing a SyntaxError on import.
steps_to_reproduce: Start the Rag_Chatbot service (uvicorn main:app).
expected: Service starts normally.
actual: ImportError/SyntaxError before the app can even load.

title: Mentor CV upload always crashes with a 500
description: pdfjs-dist 6.x explicitly rejects Node Buffer instances (requires a plain Uint8Array) in services/pdfTextService.js, but multer's memoryStorage() always hands the controller a real Buffer.
steps_to_reproduce: POST a real PDF to /api/mentors/:mentorId/cv as the owning mentor.
expected: 200, CV parsed and profile updated.
actual: 500 'Failed to parse CV' on every single request, regardless of PDF validity.

title: AI_interviewer's mentee CSV export always crashes once any profile exists
description: export_csv() in services/interview_service.py passed session_id to MenteeProfile(...) both explicitly and via a dict-comprehension spread, causing 'got multiple values for keyword argument'.
steps_to_reproduce: Complete at least one AI interview, then GET /export/mentees.csv.
expected: 200, CSV file with header + one row per completed profile.
actual: 500 TypeError on every call once >=1 profile exists.

title: Real production MongoDB Atlas credentials hardcoded as a fallback default in source
description: backend/AI_interviewer/core/config.py:36 hardcodes the exact same username/password as the real MONGO_URI in backend/.env as a fallback default for os.getenv(). Confirmed via git log -p this fallback was introduced replacing an earlier safe localhost default. .env itself is gitignored, but this literal is tracked in git history.
steps_to_reproduce: git log -p backend/AI_interviewer/core/config.py, or simply read the file: `mongo_uri=os.getenv("MONGO_URI", "mongodb+srv://prolignco_db_user:...@prolign.s3kf9zd.mongodb.net/...")`.
expected: No real credentials ever appear in a fallback default or anywhere in git history; a missing MONGO_URI should fail loudly, not silently connect to production.
actual: Anyone with repo/clone access has live Atlas credentials. If MONGO_URI is ever unset in any environment, the app silently connects to the production cluster.

title: POST /api/payments lets a client fabricate a fully 'captured' payment with an arbitrary amount, bypassing Stripe
description: services/paymentService.js createPayment() takes grossAmount, chargeStatus, and stripePaymentIntentId straight from the request body with no cross-check against the session's real price or any actual Stripe confirmation.
steps_to_reproduce: As any mentee, POST /api/payments with { sessionId, grossAmount: 0.01, chargeStatus: 'captured' }.
expected: Payment amount/status should be derived from a real, server-verified Stripe charge, never trusted from the client.
actual: The session gets paymentId set as if a real charge for the client-chosen amount succeeded — no Stripe call is ever made.

title: POST /api/sessions accepts a client-supplied priceCharged that overrides the mentor's real price
description: services/sessionService.js:162 uses `body.priceCharged ?? profile?.pricePerSession ?? profile?.hourlyRate ?? 0` — a client-sent priceCharged always wins over the mentor's actual configured price, and Session.priceCharged has no min bound in the schema. This value later drives the real Stripe charge amount in createPaymentIntent.
steps_to_reproduce: As any mentee, POST /api/sessions with { mentorId, slotId, sessionType, priceCharged: 0 } (or a negative number).
expected: priceCharged should be a server-computed snapshot of the mentor's real price, never accepted from the client, and schema-bounded to >= 0.
actual: The session (and any resulting Stripe charge) is created at whatever price the mentee chooses, including 0 or negative.

title: POST /api/interview/complete-ai silently discards interview data by writing to non-existent schema fields
description: services/interviewService.js completeInterview() (lines 73-104) $set's keys like education, careerGoals, domainInterest, softSkills, skillProfile, onboardingAnswers, interviewAnswers — none of which exist on the Mentee_Profiles schema (which uses snake_case: domain_interest, target_role, tech_skills, etc.). Mongoose's default strict:true silently drops unknown paths.
steps_to_reproduce: Call POST /api/interview/complete-ai with a full menteeRecord payload as a logged-in mentee.
expected: All submitted fields (career goals, skills, target role, etc.) persist to the mentee's profile.
actual: Only university/degree/bio/userId (fields that happen to also exist on the schema) persist. Everything else is silently discarded with no error.

title: Login for a Google-only account crashes with 500 and leaks an account-enumeration signal
description: A Google-signup user never gets a password set. Logging in with any password calls bcrypt.compare(password, undefined), which rejects with an uncaught, statusCode-less error -> the global error handler returns 500 with the raw bcrypt message, instead of the app's usual generic 401.
steps_to_reproduce: Sign up via Google OAuth, then POST /api/auth/login for that same email with any password.
expected: 401 'Invalid email or password' — identical to every other wrong-credential case, per the app's own anti-enumeration design.
actual: 500 Internal Server Error with a distinct bcrypt error message, revealing this account has no local password.

title: createPaymentIntent has no amount validation and no pre-check before calling Stripe, risking duplicate PaymentIntents
description: Unlike createPayment, createPaymentIntent (services/paymentService.js:124-167) never validates session.priceCharged (NaN/negative/zero all pass through raw) and never checks for an existing Payment before calling Stripe — it relies entirely on a DB unique index that only fires AFTER the Stripe API call.
steps_to_reproduce: Double-click 'Pay' (or fire two concurrent requests) for the same session's create-intent endpoint.
expected: Only one Stripe PaymentIntent is ever created per session; invalid amounts are rejected before reaching Stripe.
actual: Two concurrent requests can each successfully create a separate Stripe PaymentIntent; only one Payment record saves locally, leaving an orphaned, chargeable PaymentIntent.

title: Double-booking race condition on recurring availability slots
description: services/sessionService.js's rec- slotId booking path (lines 97-124) does a non-atomic read-then-write (check existingConcrete.status, then save) instead of the atomic findOneAndUpdate used by the one-off slot path a few lines below.
steps_to_reproduce: Fire two concurrent POST /api/sessions requests against the same recurring-template slot/date.
expected: Only one booking succeeds; the second gets a 409.
actual: Both requests can read status:available before either write lands, and both create a Session for the same slot.

title: Google OAuth successful login redirects to a malformed double-slash URL, breaking the entire flow
description: authController.js builds `new URL(`${env.FRONTEND_URL}/auth/callback`)`. The current .env FRONTEND_URL has a trailing slash, producing pathname '//auth/callback', which the React Router route registered as '/auth/callback' does not match. The OAuth failure-redirect path (routes/auth.js) has the same issue plus uses unvalidated process.env.FRONTEND_URL directly (no fallback if unset).
steps_to_reproduce: Complete a real Google OAuth login with the current .env configuration.
expected: Browser lands on /auth/callback and completes login.
actual: Browser is redirected to a URL the frontend router can't match (404/blank page) — Google login does not complete.

title: Conflicting index definitions on Mentee_Profiles.session_id between Node and Python
description: backend/models/Mentee_Profiles.js declares session_id as a plain (non-unique) indexed field, auto-creating index 'session_id_1'. backend/AI_interviewer/services/interview_service.py separately creates a UNIQUE index with the same default name on the same physical collection.
steps_to_reproduce: Start both the Node backend and the AI_interviewer service against the same database and inspect the Mentee_Profiles collection's indexes.
expected: One consistent index definition (unique or not) agreed on by both services.
actual: Whichever service creates its index second gets an IndexOptionsConflict, and the two services disagree on whether session_id should be unique.

title: MentorProfile has no index on the actual hot-path filter field (status), but carries a dead compound index
description: MentorProfile.js defines index({isApproved:1, isActive:1}) — but isActive does not exist anywhere in the schema, and isApproved is never used as a query filter anywhere in the codebase. Meanwhile every real mentor listing query (/api/mentors, /recommended, /:id) filters on status, which has no index at all.
steps_to_reproduce: Review MentorProfile.js's index definitions against the actual $match filters in mentorService.js's mentorPipeline/getMentorById/listMentorProfiles.
expected: An index supporting the status filter that every browse/listing query actually uses.
actual: The platform's primary mentor-browsing feature forces a collection scan at any real scale; the maintained index provides zero read benefit.

title: Rag_Chatbot has zero indexes on conversations/escalations, hit on every single chat turn
description: A full search of backend/Rag_Chatbot for create_index/createIndex returns no matches, despite conversation_selector.get_recent_messages and escalation_selector.find_pending being queried on every POST /chat and every GET /history/{session_id} call.
steps_to_reproduce: Review backend/Rag_Chatbot/app/selector/*.py's query filters against the conversations/escalations collections' actual indexes.
expected: Indexes on at least session_id (and created_at for the history query) on both collections.
actual: Every chat turn and history fetch does an unindexed collection scan, which will not scale.

title: No cascade cleanup on User deletion — dangling references across Session/Payment/Review/AvailabilitySlot
description: adminService.deleteUser() and userService.deleteAccount() cascade only to MentorProfile/MenteeProfileFlat. Session, Payment, Review, AvailabilitySlot, Notification, and ChatMessage documents referencing the deleted user's ObjectId are never touched.
steps_to_reproduce: As an admin, delete a mentor who has a confirmed future Session with a linked Payment.
expected: Either the deletion is blocked while active sessions exist, or dependent records are cleaned up/flagged.
actual: The Session, its AvailabilitySlot (still marked booked), and any linked Payment/Review all keep referencing a User._id that no longer exists, with no clean way to cancel/refund through normal flows.

title: Analytics page crashes for every mentor and admin — missing useEffect import
description: frontend/src/pages/Analytics.jsx only imports {useMemo, useState} from React, but its internal AnimatedNumber component (used by KPICard, rendered 16 times on page load) calls useEffect.
steps_to_reproduce: As a mentor or admin, navigate to /analytics.
expected: Analytics dashboard renders with KPI cards and animated counters.
actual: ReferenceError: useEffect is not defined — caught by the route-level ErrorBoundary, showing a generic 'Something went wrong' panel instead of the page. Analytics is 100% unusable for 2 of 3 roles.

title: Mentor dashboard earnings/analytics bucket every session into 'today' due to malformed date parsing
description: MentorDashboard.jsx's parseSessionDate concatenates an ISO datetime string with a time-range string ('2026-08-01T14:00:00.000Z 02:00 PM - 03:00 PM'), producing an Invalid Date. The code then falls back to session.createdAt, which is never actually set on the mapped session objects, so it falls back again to Date.now() for every session.
steps_to_reproduce: As a mentor with historical sessions, open the Earnings tab or Sessions Analytics sub-tab and filter by a past week/month/year.
expected: Sessions filtered and charted by their real scheduledDate.
actual: Every session is bucketed into the current day, so filtering to any past period shows zero sessions even when real ones exist; Revenue Trend/Monthly Breakdown and the CSV export are all corrupted the same way. (MenteeDashboard.jsx does this correctly — the fix wasn't copied over.)

title: GET /api/reviews/:id has no visibility or ownership check, bypassing moderation
description: listReviews correctly filters {isVisible:true, flagged:false} for public browsing, but getReview(id) (services/reviewService.js:92-96) applies no such filter, and the route only uses optionalAuth (no login required at all).
steps_to_reproduce: Obtain any review's ObjectId (e.g. one an admin has since hidden/flagged), GET /api/reviews/:id as a guest or unrelated user.
expected: A flagged/hidden review, or another user's private non-anonymous review, should not be readable this way.
actual: The review is returned in full regardless of visibility/flag state or who's asking.

title: CV-upload validation errors return an inconsistent response shape and the wrong HTTP status
description: multer's fileFilter/file-size-limit errors in middleware/cvUpload.js fire before cvController's own try/catch, so they skip its {error:'...'} response format and fall through to the global error handler, which returns {success:false, message} with a default 500 instead of 400.
steps_to_reproduce: POST a non-PDF file, or a PDF over 5MB, to /api/mentors/:mentorId/cv.
expected: A consistent 400 response with a clear client-error message.
actual: 500 Internal Server Error, and a different JSON shape than the same endpoint's other error paths.

title: Two-column PDF text-extraction heuristic corrupts single-column resumes
description: services/pdfTextService.js unconditionally splits every page into a left/right column by horizontal midpoint and concatenates left-then-right. Any single-column resume with right-aligned dates (a very common layout) gets those dates pulled out of each job entry and dumped together at the end of the page.
steps_to_reproduce: Upload a single-column resume with a 'Job Title, Company ......... right-aligned dates' line pattern.
expected: Text extracted in natural reading order, dates staying associated with their job entry.
actual: Dates are disconnected from their company/title, degrading the CV parser's workExperience extraction for a large share of real-world resumes.

title: Rag_Chatbot reads FRONTEND_ORIGIN but .env only defines FRONTEND_URL — CORS allowlist silently stale
description: backend/Rag_Chatbot/app/core/config.py reads os.getenv('FRONTEND_ORIGIN', 'http://localhost:5173'); no FRONTEND_ORIGIN key exists anywhere in backend/.env (only FRONTEND_URL, which the Node backend correctly reads). Works today only because the hardcoded fallback happens to match localhost dev.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy with a real (non-localhost) FRONTEND_URL configured in .env, and inspect the chatbot's CORS allowlist.
expected: The chatbot's CORS allowlist includes the real deployed frontend origin.
actual: The allowlist silently keeps using the stale localhost:5173 default, and the deployed frontend's chat requests get rejected by CORS.

title: Deleting a Session doesn't clean up its linked Payment or Review
description: sessionService.deleteSession() frees the AvailabilitySlot correctly but never deletes or unlinks the Payment (unique index on sessionId) or Review (unique index on sessionId) pointing at it. Contrast with reviewService.deleteReview(), which does correctly null out Session.reviewId.
steps_to_reproduce: As a participant, DELETE /api/sessions/:id for a session that already has a Payment and/or Review.
expected: Dependent Payment/Review records are cleaned up or clearly flagged as orphaned.
actual: Payment/Review records become permanently orphaned, with sessionId pointing at nothing, breaking financial reconciliation.

title: mentee_experience_years is always 0 for every AI-interview-sourced mentee profile
description: Mentor_Mentee_Match/datacleaning.py's encode_experience_level only recognizes 'entry'/'mid'/'senior' substrings, but the AI interview's system prompt (and the schema enum) only ever emits 'beginner'/'intermediate'/'advanced'.
steps_to_reproduce: Complete the AI mentee interview and inspect the resulting Mentee_Profiles document's mentee_experience_years field.
expected: A real numeric experience-years value derived from the mentee's stated experience level.
actual: Always 0, for every single interview-sourced profile, silently degrading the mentor-matching experience filter for 100% of mentees.

title: hourlyRate has no min bound, unlike its sibling field pricePerSession
description: MentorProfile.js: hourlyRate has no schema-level bound, while pricePerSession (used for the exact same purpose) has min:0.
steps_to_reproduce: PATCH /api/mentor-profiles/me with {hourlyRate: -100} as the owning mentor.
expected: Rejected by schema validation, matching pricePerSession's behavior.
actual: Succeeds, producing a negative price that sorts/displays incorrectly in mentor listings.

title: Raw ISO timestamps shown to users instead of formatted dates in dashboards
description: 5 render locations across MentorDashboard.jsx (lines ~749, ~1245, ~1526) and MenteeDashboard.jsx (~750, ~1874) display the raw backend ISO datetime string directly instead of the already-computed human-readable date field used everywhere else in the same components.
steps_to_reproduce: As a mentor or mentee with an upcoming/pending session, view the dashboard's Upcoming Sessions, the Sessions tab table, or a session detail/notes modal.
expected: A readable date like 'Aug 1, 2026'.
actual: A raw string like '2026-08-01T14:00:00.000Z' is shown to the user.

title: Resuming a pending-payment booking can silently swap or blank the displayed time slot
description: Booking.jsx's mentor.id effect re-fetches only status:available slots (excluding the mentee's own already-booked slot), and the auto-select effect then overwrites the correct selectedSlot with a different available slot (or null) because the real booked slot isn't in that 'available' list.
steps_to_reproduce: Book a session (creating it as pending), leave without paying, then return via 'Complete Payment' from the dashboard.
expected: The payment screen shows the originally booked time slot.
actual: The booking summary shows a different time than the session actually being paid for, or '—' for time (the underlying charge/session record is still correct, but the confirmation shown to the user is wrong).

title: Leaked duplicate session countdown timer in the video call lobby
description: VideoInterview.jsx calls calculateTimeRemaining(data) directly inside a fetch .then() rather than inside a useEffect; its internal setInterval's cleanup function is created but never invoked since it isn't returned from a useEffect. A second, correctly-written useEffect runs an identical timer alongside it.
steps_to_reproduce: Open /video-interview/:sessionId, then navigate away or close the tab before the session ends.
expected: The countdown interval is cleared on unmount.
actual: An orphaned setInterval keeps firing every second until the session's scheduled end time, even after the component unmounts; repeated visits stack up more leaked intervals.

title: clearAllSlots leaves the UI out of sync with the backend on partial failure
description: AvailabilityScheduler.jsx's clearAllSlots fires all deletes concurrently via Promise.all; if any one slot is already booked (409 from the backend), Promise.all rejects immediately even though the OTHER deletes already succeeded server-side, and local state is never updated to remove them.
steps_to_reproduce: As a mentor with 2+ slots on a day (at least one already booked), click 'Clear all slots for this day.'
expected: Slots that were actually deleted disappear from the UI; a clear message indicates which slot(s) blocked the rest.
actual: Successfully-deleted slots keep showing as still configured until the next full page refetch; the error message doesn't say which slots succeeded.

title: A pending/rejected mentor's profile is readable by any authenticated stranger
description: mentorService.getMentorProfile() (used by GET /api/mentor-profiles/:id) has no status/visibility check at all — TC-MPROFILE-004 in the QA test case CSV describes the intended 403 for a non-owner, non-admin viewer, which is not implemented.
steps_to_reproduce: As any logged-in mentee/mentor, GET /api/mentor-profiles/:id for a mentor profile whose status is pending or rejected.
expected: 403 'This profile is not public.'
actual: 200 — the full profile (including fields not meant to be public yet) is returned.

title: A mentor can self-escalate their own status, or edit any other mentor's profile, via mentor-profiles endpoints
description: POST /api/mentor-profiles and PATCH /api/mentor-profiles/:id (mentorService.js createMentorProfile/updateMentorProfile) accept arbitrary body fields with no whitelist (status/isApproved/averageRating included), and PATCH has no ownership check at all — any mentor/admin caller can edit any mentor profile by id.
steps_to_reproduce: As a mentor, POST /api/mentor-profiles with {status:'approved'}, or PATCH another mentor's profile id with {bio:'hijacked'}.
expected: status/isApproved/averageRating should be admin-only fields; PATCH should be restricted to the profile's own owner (or an admin).
actual: Both requests succeed — a mentor can self-approve, and any mentor can edit any other mentor's profile document.

title: Rag_Chatbot's known-email field is never forwarded to escalation handlers
description: agent/orchestrator.py's route(session_id, message, email) accepts an email parameter but never passes it to handler(session_id, message) — every escalation-triggering tool (escalate_complaint, handle_abusive_message, answer_faq's unanswered-FAQ path) always sees email=None on the first turn, even when the frontend already sent a known email.
steps_to_reproduce: POST /chat with a complaint-style message and email already set to a known address in the request body.
expected: The escalation should finalize immediately (post to Slack, save as notified) since the email is already known.
actual: The reply still asks the user to share their email, identical to a user with no known email at all — the field has zero effect on behavior.

title: AI_interviewer reads MONGO_DB_NAME but .env defines MONGODB_DB_NAME
description: backend/AI_interviewer/core/config.py reads os.getenv('MONGO_DB_NAME', 'Prolign'), but backend/.env defines MONGODB_DB_NAME — the names don't match, so the env var is silently ignored and the hardcoded 'Prolign' default is always used.
steps_to_reproduce: Set MONGODB_DB_NAME in .env to a different database name and restart AI_interviewer.
expected: The service connects to the configured database.
actual: The service always connects to 'Prolign' regardless of what MONGODB_DB_NAME is set to (harmless today only because that default happens to be correct).

title: Broken avatar images in Admin views for users with no profile photo
description: AdminDashboard.jsx's normalizeAdminUser sets avatar:'' when no photo exists, and the Members table, Applications list, and member-detail modal all render with no fallback — every other avatar usage in the app falls back to a ui-avatars.com/initials placeholder.
steps_to_reproduce: As an admin, view the Members list, Applications (pending mentor) list, or a member-detail modal for any user without a profile photo.
expected: A placeholder avatar (initials or ui-avatars.com), matching every other avatar in the app.
actual: A broken image icon.
